rising.description: Open-source, local-first social media research agent for Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn. Jev routes read-only steps; socai CLI captures cited browser evidence.
rising.summary: Local-first research agent that uses an LLM to choose read-only steps, such as searching, opening posts or profiles and reading comments on Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn. The socai CLI runs them in the user's signed-in Chrome and returns cited evidence for reports.
strengths: Local-first design with read-only operations and documented data flow
Produces source-cited reports with recorded example output
Open source with a tests badge and a stated release version
risks: Runs through the user's logged-in browser sessions, which raises platform terms and account-safety concerns
Profile and comment extraction could be used to build dossiers on individuals
Heavy reliance on a separate socai CLI and an OpenRouter key

rising.description: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view — and shows its work. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.
rising.summary: An agent skill that geolocates photos by combining EXIF and OCR, reverse image search, OpenStreetMap corridors, elevation skylines, sun position, satellite and street-view matching, and reports its reasoning as evidence.
strengths: Clear multi-stage pipeline with named scripts and data sources
Shows its work with evidence overlays
Works across several agent platforms with setup instructions
risks: Geolocating photos may be misused to locate private places or people
Depends on Chrome/Chromium and external services for reverse image search

rising.description: 🔎 Username, email & phone OSINT — 9,700+ lookup checks from 19 projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs and expert-reviewed updates.
rising.summary: Consensus is a Python CLI and GUI that runs username, email and phone lookups across about 9,700 site modules from 19 open-source projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs, PDF reports and an MCP server for AI assistants.
strengths: Large consolidated module set with a stated review process
Windows installer, PyPI package and source install options
Evidence graph and PDF reporting for investigations
risks: Mass username and email lookups can enable profiling of private individuals
Claims of weekly expert review are unverified marketing

rising.description: Wireshark for the radio spectrum: channelize a wide span once, decode every signal in it at once
rising.summary: Desktop SDR tool that channelizes a wide radio band and decodes many signal types at once, including ISM devices, ADS-B, AIS, APRS, pagers, DMR, TETRA, LoRa and radiosondes, with recording and an agent option.
strengths: Decodes many protocols from one wide-band capture
Named decoders and bands with a clear install path
Passive reception of public transmissions
risks: Intercepting TETRA and DMR traffic with decryption and key recovery raises legal concerns
Records voice and messages, which may capture private communications
Agent can transmit on radio, requiring licensing awareness

rising.description: Continuously updated catalogue of open-source OSINT tools, skills, plugins, MCP servers, and agentic integrations.
rising.summary: A continuously updated, hand-reviewed catalogue of OSINT tools, MCP servers, agent skills and agentic integrations, organised by category and by target input, with a CSV database.
strengths: Large organised catalogue of about 495 projects
Browsable by category and by target input
Maintained with recent update badge
risks: Catalogue content is only a list; tools are not verified by this entry
Includes social-media lookup categories that may enable profile extraction

rising.description: Open-source intelligence and human-rights hub on North Korea: intel map, missile test explorer, leadership graph, camps and verified data.
rising.summary: Open-source hub on North Korea offering an intel map with satellite layers, camp and missile site data, a missile test explorer, leadership graph, sanctions info and 28 open datasets, each point sourced.
strengths: Sourced data with weekly refresh workflow
Satellite imagery layers and open datasets
Multilingual and Apache 2.0 licensed
risks: Human-rights advocacy framing may affect neutrality of data
Limited detail on methodology for some layers

rising.description: Watchdog (branding subject to change) is an open-source intelligence (OSINT) case management platform for small teams.
rising.summary: Watchdog is a TypeScript case management platform for OSINT investigations. It keeps a single graph per case, treats collector output as proposals a person must accept, and includes org-scoped tenancy for small teams. It is pre-1.0 and not hardened for production.
strengths: Human-in-the-loop acceptance of machine results keeps provenance defensible
Clear architecture stack and documented differences from MISP, TheHive, and IntelOwl
risks: Pre-1.0 with schemas and APIs changing without notice
README excerpt gives limited detail on concrete data sources or collectors

rising.description: Free alternative to https://osint-ui.com
rising.summary: A free, browser-based suite of about 20 OSINT tools covering username, email, breach, password-hash, DNS and certificate lookups, with a FastAPI backend for some tools. Positioned as a free alternative to osint-ui.com.
strengths: Many tools with named free public data sources
Browser-first design keeps analysed files local
Explicit passive-only stance and documented data sources
risks: Username and email lookups can support personal-data inference
Licence combines Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause, limiting commercial use
Readme digest is truncated, so some tool details are unverified

rising.description: Who's being heard, not just who's talking. Public social posts of candidates in the 2026 Czech municipal elections across ten cities, collected with Apify into a DuckDB evidence graph and mapped in a static app.
rising.summary: Starwatch collects public social media posts from verified 2026 Czech municipal election candidates via Apify into a DuckDB graph, then displays reach, posts and 2022 results in a static map app.
strengths: Documented pipeline from official registry to static app
Explicit attribution verification and links back to sources
Clear legal note on excluding polls and forecasts
risks: Profiling of named political candidates' social accounts
Snapshot-based, tied to a single hackathon period

rising.description: Strażnik — nieoficjalne wczesne ostrzeganie o zagrożeniach powietrznych dla Polski. Fuzja sygnałów NEPTUN, mediów, RCB, ADS-B i PAŻP + aplikacja Android.
rising.summary: Unofficial early-warning tool for Poland that fuses NEPTUN, media, RCB, ADS-B and PAŻP airspace signals into a map with an Android app, backend on FastAPI and documented scoring and alerts.
strengths: Multiple named public data sources fused into one picture
Detailed release notes and user manual
Documents limits and scoring rules
risks: Alert accuracy depends on unofficial sources; possible false reassurance or panic
Hosted on a personal server with unclear long-term maintenance

rising.description: apt for OSINT tools (package manager)
rising.summary: OTinstaller is a command-line package manager for OSINT tools. It installs, runs, updates and removes tools such as Sherlock and Maigret by name, each in its own virtualenv, with typed inputs for usernames, emails and domains, and saves results with metadata.
strengths: Clear working CLI with install, run, update and remove commands
Per-tool virtualenv isolation and saved results with SHA-256 metadata
Documented install paths and tested platforms
risks: Wraps third-party tools, so its safety depends on those upstream projects
README is largely quick-start material with limited detail on data sources or legal considerations

rising.description: Local-first privacy toolkit. Map yourself against 400+ data brokers, send CCPA/GDPR deletion mail, and check password dumps — the vault never leaves your PC.
rising.summary: Local-first privacy toolkit that matches your own name, email and phone against 400+ people-search and marketing data brokers, queues CCPA/GDPR deletion emails, and checks passwords against public Pwned Passwords ranges, storing everything in a local vault.
strengths: Local-first design with no account and an encrypted local vault
Clear description of k-anonymity password check limiting data sent
Explicit about what the tool does not do
risks: Self-lookup on people-search sites could be repurposed to look up others
Relies on a maintained broker catalog that may go stale

rising.description: Real-time tactical OSINT & GEOINT dashboard. Live flight tracking (ADS-B), maritime vessels, satellites, undersea telecom cables & HUD shaders powered by free, keyless open APIs.
rising.summary: Open-source tactical dashboard showing live ADS-B aircraft, AIS vessels, satellites, public traffic cameras, earthquakes, and undersea cables on 2D and 3D maps, using free keyless APIs.
strengths: Named public data sources with endpoints listed
Keyless, runnable locally with clear quick-start steps
Explicit disclaimer and honest labelling of non-live data
risks: Marketing-heavy README with some unsupported superlatives
Limited detail on legal considerations for camera feed aggregation

rising.description: An OSINT investigation case mapping tool for organizing entities, relationships, evidence, and intelligence.
rising.summary: A browser-based OSINT case file tool that maps people, identifiers, relationships, locations and timelines, with evidence hashing, chain of custody, audit logs, and report export. Runs fully client-side.
strengths: Fully client-side with no telemetry
SHA-256 evidence hashing and chain of custody
Includes fictional sample case and Docker setup
risks: Stores subject photos and personal identifiers, including breach records and social platform entries
Derived from OSINTMapper; attribution present but modified fork

rising.description: A responsible, open-source Instagram username availability scanner. Async CLI with bounded concurrency, rate-limit backoff, resumable scans, Docker and GitHub Actions support.
rising.summary: Async Python CLI that generates short Instagram usernames and checks public profile pages to flag names with no visible profile. Supports rate-limit backoff, resumable scans, and txt, json, or csv output. Results are candidates only and must be verified on Instagram.
strengths: Documents clear limitations and that results are not guaranteed claimable
Resumable checkpoints and conservative UNKNOWN classification
Concrete example run and multiple output formats
risks: Brute-force enumeration of platform accounts may conflict with Instagram terms of service
Usefulness for OSINT is limited; mainly a username availability tool
Scope is contestable since the purpose is registration availability rather than investigation

rising.description: ⚒️ Open-source OSINT and digital forensics skills for AI assistants. Investigate sources, challenge hypotheses, analyze artifacts, and produce evidence-referenced reports with portable case files and offline Python tools. Designed for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI.
rising.summary: A set of 16 OSINT and digital forensics skills for AI assistants (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI). It turns documents, captures and logs into portable cases with preserved evidence, referenced findings, and offline Python tools for review and reporting.
strengths: Preserves original evidence with byte checks and source references
Offline Python standard-library runtime with no telemetry
Multiple export formats including GraphML and EN/FR reports
risks: Depends on host assistant models and their data transmission
Benchmark claims are limited by the project's own trials

rising.description: Export the complete follower list of any public X (Twitter) account to CSV + JSONL.
rising.summary: Python CLI that uses a user's session cookies to call X's internal GraphQL API and export the full follower list of a public account to CSV and JSONL, with resume checkpoints and multi-session rotation.
strengths: Concrete usage examples and documented output files
Documents rate limits and resume checkpoint behaviour
Clear flags and maintenance notes for rotating queryIds
risks: Uses session cookies and README admits likely violation of X Terms of Service
Relies on undocumented internal API that may break
Bulk harvesting of follower profiles raises privacy concerns

rising.description: GeoWeb — find where any photo (or video) was taken. A local-first, open-source browser console around the GeoInt recon pipeline, with Docker, docs and a GitHub Pages landing site.
rising.summary: GeoWeb is a local-first open-source browser console that estimates where a photo or video was taken, combining EXIF metadata, OCR, reverse image search, object detection, horizon calibration and learned world priors with a Docker setup and MCP server.
strengths: Runs locally with no uploads, keeping analyst in the loop
Clear quickstart and Docker instructions
Shows evidence and caveats for each candidate location
risks: Reverse image search via Yandex/Baidu may raise third-party data concerns
README excerpt lacks legal or ethical considerations section
Relatively new project with limited maturity signals

rising.description: Check simultaneously if a phone number is registered on popular apps & websites, without any prerequisite 📞
rising.summary: Go CLI and TUI that checks in parallel whether a phone number is registered on several popular apps and websites. Offers JSON output, privacy-conscious logging, and a single-target scope.
strengths: Concrete CLI usage with parallel module checks and JSON output
Privacy-conscious logging and silent-by-default modules
Cross-platform binaries and go install path
risks: Phone-number registration checks can enable targeting of private individuals
Installation section is partly unfinished (work-in-progress notes)
Legal section relies on a non-OSI internal-use license

rising.description: Offline desktop workspace for organizing OSINT investigations.
rising.summary: OpenTrace is an offline Windows/Linux desktop app (PySide6) for organizing OSINT investigations with a visual board, tasks, sources, hypotheses, journal, SHA-256 integrity info, and portable case folders. No telemetry or accounts.
strengths: Fully offline with no telemetry or accounts
Visual investigation board with relationships and exports
Tests in CI on Windows and Ubuntu
risks: Early-stage project with limited documentation of data formats
Binary release targets Windows x64 only

rising.description: OSINT toolkit for crypto investigations: trace stolen funds on Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron and Solana — CLI and local web UI
rising.summary: Python CLI and local web UI that pulls public on-chain history for Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana and TON, labels known entities, scores risk and maps fund flows for crypto theft investigations.
strengths: Covers multiple chains with named data sources
Documents limitations and heuristic caveats honestly
Offline selftest and a local web UI with fund-flow graph
risks: Relies on rate-limited public endpoints and API keys
Attribution beyond exchanges is heuristic

rising.description: OmniScope Web - 100% Serverless Static Geospatial Intelligence & Doppler Weather Radar Dashboard for Cloudflare Pages. Zero cloud database fees, zero server costs, pure open data.
rising.summary: Serverless static web dashboard for Cloudflare Pages showing live radar precipitation, USGS earthquakes, Open-Meteo weather, public webcams and ISS orbit, with an MCP server and keyless edge APIs.
strengths: Keyless, client-side design using public open data feeds
Named data sources and a documented deployment path
risks: README contains heavy promotional and trademark claims with little technical substance
Weather and webcam focus is only loosely OSINT; limited investigative use

rising.description: Ferramenta de dorking em múltiplos motores de busca para coleta de URLs em operações de OSINT e reconhecimento.
rising.summary: SimpleReconDorking runs search dorks in parallel across multiple search engines and returns the union of found URLs. Supports dork strings, files, a built-in categorised catalogue, and stdin, with Docker install and usage examples.
strengths: Clear purpose and multiple input modes
Documented usage examples and Docker setup
Built-in dork catalogue by category
risks: Dorking can be used to find exposed targets; README carries a consent warning only
Some engines require browser bypass, which may violate terms of service

rising.description: Instagram Scraper — free, open-source Instagram scraper. Unlimited profiles, posts, reels, comments and hashtags as clean JSON, no API key, no proxies.
rising.summary: A free, open-source Instagram scraper exposed as a local API that returns profile, post, reel, comment and hashtag data as JSON, with example outputs and endpoint documentation.
strengths: Working local API with curl example
Clear JSON output examples for profiles
Covers profiles, posts, comments, hashtags and locations
risks: Scraping may violate Instagram terms of service
Promotional wording like unlimited and no proxies with few stated limits
Topics include email scraping, raising personal-data concerns

rising.description: 28 OSINT Agent Skills that turn Cursor, Claude & AI coding agents into a full open-source intelligence platform — reconnaissance, attribution, GEOINT, breach checks & due diligence. Ethical, sourced, passive-first.
rising.summary: A set of 28 agent skills for Cursor and Claude that chain OSINT techniques such as WHOIS, DNS, certificate transparency, breach lookups, reverse image search and geolocation into sourced reports. Includes install script and reference material.
strengths: Broad coverage across OSINT domains with 10 workflows and 18 techniques
Emphasises passive-first methodology and sourced, confidence-rated findings
Includes install script and reference cookbooks
risks: Breach lookups and person-focused pivots could enable personal data lookup
Marketing-heavy README with illustrative rather than verified example output
Relies on third-party API keys for several tools

strengths: Clear modes (FAST/DEEP) with stated bounds
Separates observed data from inferences and notes limits
Documents privacy handling and rate limits

Optional GitLeak enrichment touches leaked-data sources

new.description: China-network workarounds for the geo-sleuth photo-geolocation skill: AMap satellite tiles, Baidu-only fast intake, evidence sheet builder
new.summary: A set of scripts that extends the geo-sleuth photo-geolocation agent skill for users on mainland China networks. It offers a Baidu-based fast intake, AMap satellite tile mosaics, offline phone-number geodata lookup, and a builder for evidence sheets. It is a companion to geo-sleu
strengths: Concrete commands and documented inputs for satellite tile mosaics
Clear lane split between China and worldwide workflows with measured timings
Offline phone-number region lookup with no network dependency
risks: Depends on the external geo-sleuth skill being installed
Some README sections are truncated and details of data handling are sparse

new.description: Open-source skills for AI agents: reverse engineer a product from public evidence, rebuild it on looot, request the data sources that are missing.
new.summary: An open-source pack of skills for AI agents that reverse engineers a product from public evidence, maps its capabilities, and rebuilds it as a small app on looot, a paid data API service. It also files requests for missing data sources.
strengths: Clear workflow that tags findings as observed, inferred or unknown
Free path needs no account and runs passively on public pages
risks: Tied to a commercial data API vendor, so the tool is a promotional funnel
Competitor teardown could be misused for copying products

new.description: A modular, command-line OSINT & Reconnaissance suite written in Python
new.summary: A Python command-line OSINT and reconnaissance suite with a menu of modules for domain and network scanning, public breach checks, IP geolocation and crypto wallet lookups. The README is brief and lacks usage detail.
strengths: Broad multi-module coverage in one CLI
Modular design with one file per tool
risks: README gives little detail on data sources, usage or limits
Marketing-style feature claims without specifics
Breach checks may touch personal data

new.description: Offline OSINT triage for saved HTML: link inventories, host summaries, line references and SHA-256 evidence hashes. Zero runtime dependencies.
new.summary: Lucerna is an offline CLI that parses saved HTML files to extract HTTP(S) links, group destination hosts, record line numbers, and hash the original bytes with SHA-256. It also compares two saved reports to show added, removed, and changed URLs and metadata.
strengths: Works fully offline with zero runtime dependencies
Clear usage examples and JSON/CSV/Markdown output formats
risks: Narrow scope limited to static HTML link inventories
Early version (0.2.0) with limited community adoption signals

new.description: Cross-platform OSINT reconnaissance: 65 social/dev/media vectors, avatar clustering, DNS/PGP enrichment, dossier export via CLI & web UI.
new.summary: Local-first Node.js reconnaissance tool that sweeps 65 platforms from a username, email or domain, adds DNS, PGP, avatar-reuse and CT enrichment, and exports a correlated identity dossier via CLI or web UI.
strengths: Zero dependencies and no API keys required
Documents runtime requirements and probe strategies
Clear ethical-use section
risks: Dossier building on individuals raises privacy and stalking concerns
Initial v1.0.0 release with limited track record
Accuracy of cross-platform correlation unverified

new.description: A Kali Linux-friendly Python CLI for public-only username checks and contact discovery on public websites.
new.summary: A Python command-line tool that checks candidate public profile URLs for a username, reads public GitHub metadata via the API, and extracts emails and phone candidates from supplied public websites, producing JSON and HTML reports.
strengths: Clear public-only limits and caveats documented
Concrete install and usage instructions for Kali Linux
Outputs structured reports with integrity digest
risks: Username-based profile checks and contact extraction target individuals
Phone candidates may belong to unrelated third parties
Example username appears to be a specific individual handle

new.description: Análisis de metadatos EXIF del reto BreadCrumbs (OSINT · The Breach · ThePwnLab, plataforma del Bootcamp de Ciberseguridad de The Bridge): reconstrucción con ExifTool de dónde y cuándo se tomaron cinco fotografías a partir de sus coordenadas GPS y marcas de tiempo.
new.summary: Write-up of a CTF OSINT challenge showing how ExifTool reveals GPS coordinates and timestamps in five photos to reconstruct a route. Mainly a learning example, not a reusable tool.
strengths: Clear step-by-step methodology with commands
Explains limits of metadata reliability
risks: CTF writeup, not a working tool
Educational content from a bootcamp context

established.description: Collaborative peer-to-peer OSINT investigation board — end-to-end encrypted, no server-side data, works offline. Desktop app for Windows & Linux.
established.summary: COSINT is an offline-capable, peer-to-peer desktop investigation board for Windows and Linux. Analysts map entities, link them, grade sources, and collaborate in real time with end-to-end encryption and no server-side storage.
strengths: Clear architecture with E2E encrypted P2P sync and no backend
Concrete features: entity taxonomy, Admiralty source grading, .trace export
Multilingual UI and offline and 100% local modes
risks: Mostly case-management tooling rather than data collection
Tests and badges are self-reported; no independent verification of claims

established.description: God's Eye View 中文版 — 浏览器里的开源空间情报三维地球，附运行时中文界面外挂与 macOS 双击启动器。Chinese localization of bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.
established.summary: A browser-based Cesium 3D globe that overlays public live feeds such as aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes and cameras, with optional voice control. This entry is the Chinese localization of bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.
strengths: Runs locally in the browser with inspectable source code
Multiple public data feeds on one globe
Clear quick-start paths including no-API-key option
risks: Localization fork; upstream project is the primary source
Marketing-heavy README with popularity claims
Some data (traffic, camera poses) is simulated or coarse

established.description: High-end Telegram OSINT Toolkit built with Telethon. Bulk keyword search, chat export, member enumeration, proxy/Tor support & SQLite. For cybersecurity & intelligence work.
established.summary: A Python CLI built on Telethon for keyword search across Telegram channels, chat and media export, member enumeration, user/channel profiling, live monitoring and SQLite storage, with proxy and Tor support.
strengths: Concrete CLI commands with example inputs and outputs
Multiple export formats and persistent SQLite storage
Includes legal and ethical notice and rate-limit awareness
risks: Member enumeration and user profiling can target private individuals
Marketing-heavy README claims such as 'High-end' and 'Production Ready' without evidence
Requires personal Telegram API credentials; no independent testing evident

established.description: Passive surveillance detection for Android — WiFi/BLE radar, Flock ALPR & Axon body camera alerts, optional ESP32 sniffer. Privacy-first local OSINT.
established.summary: MILLIE is a passive Android (Termux) and optional ESP32 CYD tool that listens to nearby WiFi and BLE signals, classifies suspicious devices such as hidden networks, cameras and police equipment, and shows a live radar dashboard with CSV export.
strengths: Passive listening with no active probing
Live radar dashboard with classification and anomaly flags
Local-first design with optional encrypted database
risks: Targets law-enforcement equipment detection, which may raise legal questions in some jurisdictions
Setup relies on curl piping a remote script into bash
Limited documentation of data sources and legal considerations

adjacent.description: Multi-agent open-source intelligence and threat analysis platform with source attribution, evidence provenance, and encrypted credential storage.
adjacent.summary: Next.js/TypeScript platform that harvests public telemetry from 74 sources, hashes raw evidence with SHA-256, validates LLM claims against citations, and runs ACH-style multi-agent hypothesis analysis with encrypted BYO-LLM key storage.
strengths: Named data sources and concrete provenance design (SHA-256 hashing, citation validation)
Clear test suite and setup instructions
risks: Heavy marketing language and self-described zero-hallucination claims without independent evidence
Sanctions screening is explicitly preliminary, not for AML compliance use

adjacent.description: Authorized blackbox recon accelerator. A Python CLI that reduces friction between recon steps, with a scope gate and an audit log on every request.
adjacent.summary: A Python CLI for authorized blackbox web recon. It adds a scope gate, audit logging, rate limits, fingerprinting from data-driven signatures, crawl and diff steps, and reports for pentesters.
strengths: Scope enforcement and audit logging on every request
Data-driven fingerprint signatures and CVE mapping
Documented install, usage and safety guardrails
risks: Active probing tool aimed at hosts, not OSINT on people
Unsafe methods available behind a flag
Offensive pentest tooling with CVE mapping

adjacent.description: Remove metadata from photos, PDFs, Office documents, audio and video. Strips EXIF, GPS location, camera serial numbers, author names and timestamps. A desktop app and command-line tool, written in Rust, that works offline.
adjacent.summary: Offline Rust desktop app and CLI that finds and strips hidden metadata such as EXIF, GPS, camera serials and author names from photos, PDFs, Office documents, audio and video before sharing.
strengths: Works fully offline with no network code paths
Clear CLI usage with show and strip commands
Discloses known limitations and past bugs
risks: Status 0.2.0 with no external audit
Metadata removal is a privacy tool rather than investigation

adjacent.description: Real-time situational-awareness dashboard for Hong Kong - one map, many official open data sources, no API keys in the client. Open source (AGPL-3.0); not a government system.
adjacent.summary: Browser-based live map of Hong Kong combining official open data sources such as traffic cameras, weather, transport, border wait times and aircraft positions, with a whitelist Cloudflare Worker proxy and scenario modes.
strengths: Documented, traceable public data sources with attribution
No API keys or accounts in the client
Clear scenario modes and live feeds
risks: OSINT is only one feature of a civic information dashboard
Includes a not-government disclaimer but no legal analysis of camera use shown in excerpt

adjacent.description: CRS-01 — Cannabis Research Sentinel. Graph-first intelligence layer for cannabis breeding knowledge: evidence-backed strain lineage with honest trust tiers.
adjacent.summary: CRS-01 researches cannabis strain lineage across the open web, extracts parent-strain claims with a hybrid LLM and regex extractor, and stores them in a SQLite knowledge graph with source-attributed trust tiers.
strengths: Every claim is attributable to a source URL with provenance
Trust tiers are derived from evidence agreement, not asserted
Clear write boundaries and documented architecture
risks: Narrow domain; not a general OSINT investigation tool
Relies on LLM extraction which may produce errors
Scope is niche relative to OSINT index criteria

adjacent.description: Fast, dependency-free Python CLI for passive domain reconnaissance, multi-platform username hunting (56+ sites), OpSec proxies, and local AI (Ollama) threat synthesis.
adjacent.summary: Python CLI using only the standard library for passive domain reconnaissance (DNS, email anti-spoofing), multi-platform username search across 56+ sites, optional proxy routing, Shodan/VirusTotal/Censys lookups, and Ollama-based local AI briefings.
strengths: Zero external dependencies
Clear documented modes for username and domain recon
Passive-by-design stated with export formats
risks: Username hunting can enable profiling of individuals
Platform count claims not independently verified in digest

adjacent.description: ptrclassify is a small, dependency-free Python library and CLI that infers likely IP usage and location from reverse-DNS PTR hostnames
adjacent.summary: A dependency-free Python library and CLI that heuristically labels IP addresses from reverse-DNS PTR hostnames, inferring allocation, access type, hosting provider, and location with confidence scores and matched rule IDs. Optional Hyperscan engine and FastAPI service.
strengths: Explicitly heuristic, with confidence scores and rule IDs for transparency
Multiple usage paths: library, CLI, CSV enrichment, and API
Documented label taxonomy and installable from PyPI
risks: PTR naming is operator-controlled, so labels may be wrong
Location inference from hostnames could be misused for tracking individuals' IPs
Legal and ethical limits of IP attribution are not discussed in the excerpt

adjacent.description: PWN//NET is an ethical bug-hunting and networking toolkit designed for  researchers, and enthusiasts. From identifying critical vulnerabilities to uncovering hidden attack surfaces, PWN//NET equips you with 45+ real-world scanners and diagnostic tools.
adjacent.summary: A web and Android toolkit bundling about 47 security tools: web crawler, subdomain enumeration, JS secrets scanner, CORS audit, dork tool, WordPress scanner, Have I Been Pwned check, port scanning, hash cracker and payload studio, plus reference sheets.
strengths: Broad set of named tools with a web UI
